messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: elevated error rate detected in prod-eu-west (svc: inference-gateway). 5xx rate > 8% over 2m, 429s rising. Root cause suspected: recent rate/quota policy change applied 00:58 UTC. Query: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"gateway\",status=~\"5..\"}[2m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"gateway\"}[2m])) * 100`

alice: oncall here, seeing the page. pulling up dashboards now — gimme 60s to confirm impact and blast radius. :phone:

bob: looking at logs, noticing a flood of upstream timeouts from model-proxy with `context deadline exceeded` starting at 00:59:05 UTC. 429s are coming from our quota-service returning `quota_exceeded` for some clients then gateway retries turning into 5xx.

charlie: fwiw we rolled a quota policy change at 00:58 (PR #4521) that tightened burst windows for a subset of tenants. i suspected this could be risky at high-concurrency but tests passed.

dana: support seeing customer tickets and real-time stream shows multiple high-traffic tenants with aborted requests. customer-success flagged 3 enterprise customers with >50% error rate.

elaine: metric snapshots: p95 latency jumped from 420ms to 1.9s; request volume steady. backend error budget alarms are tripped.

alice: initial mitigation plan: 1) disable the new quota rule (rollback) 2) enable temporary permissive fallback policy in quota-service 3) disable gateway retries for quota errors to avoid amplification 4) scale up model-proxy pool by +30% for EU region. I'll execute 1 and 2 now.

bob: agree. also temp disable aggressive retry loop in proxy while we stabilize — I can push a config change.

charlie: rolling back the quota rule now (command):
```
# rollback PR 4521
kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/quota-service --to-revision=4519
```
Rolling...

incident-bot: Deploy started: rollback/quota-service (by charlie) — status: in_progress.

alice: toggled permissive fallback in quota-service (feature flag: permissive-mode=true). setting SLO: keep 5xx < 2% and 429s decreasing.

bob: disabling gateway retry-on-429 in env config: `GATEWAY_RETRY_ON_QUOTA=false` and restarting 3/3 gateway pods.

incident-bot: Gateway pods restart triggered by bob — pod restarts: 3.

charlie: rollback confirmed complete; quota-service back to previous policy at 01:03:12 UTC. metrics trending — 429s stopped spiking for some tenants.

elaine: graphs show 429 rate starting to decline at 01:04, but we still have elevated 5xx (around 3.5%). looks like retry amplification created a backlog at model-proxy leading to timeouts.

bob: scaled model-proxy deployment in eu-west to 1.3x (from 20 -> 26 replicas) to chew the backlog. command: `kubectl scale deploy/model-proxy --replicas=26 -n prod-eu-west`

alice: I've notified CS and flagged impacted customers. dana — can you post a short customer-facing note and ask for logs/IDs from three flagged customers? we need request IDs to do per-tenant debug.

dana: on it. posting to the affected customers Slack workspaces and opening support tickets. asking for request IDs and approximate times (00:58-01:06 UTC).

frank: CS update: Customers A and B reported partial outages for inference endpoints; they shifted traffic to backups and are seeing degraded but usable results. asking for ETA to resolution.

alice: current ETA: 20-30m to return to baseline if backlog drains. keeping pagers up.

incident-bot: Metrics poll at 01:07 UTC: 5xx = 3.1%, 429 = 0.4%, p95 latency = 1.2s.

bob: digging into proxy logs, we see many `upstream reset` events correlated with high concurrency from a set of client API keys. adding temporary IP-based shaping for those clients to protect the fleet.

charlie: applying rate-shaping rule (temporary) — `traffic-shaper apply --selector tenants=high-throughput --max-rps=50`

alice: good. also enabling a temporary canary fallback: Route non-critical requests to smaller model variant to lower inference time. Patch applied and rolling: `route-control set --route /v1/generate --model=small-v2 --weight=0.25`

elaine: after shaping + routing changes, p95 fell to 750ms at 01:15 and 5xx to ~1.6%. backlog draining.

dana: support: customers acknowledged mitigations and appreciate frequent updates. two customers requested a post-incident follow-up for SLA credits.

frank: capturing timelines for CS: root cause: quota policy tightening + gateway retry amplification causing proxy backlog -> timeouts (5xx). Impact: multiple enterprise tenants saw high error rates and degraded performance for ~17 minutes (peak window).

alice: next steps / action items: - postmortem entry and root-cause analysis (charlie + bob) - add integration test that simulates quota enforcement under burst traffic (devex + eng-ml) - add circuit-breaker in gateway to avoid retry amplification (bob) - improve deploy gating for quota policy PRs (release) - validate alerting thresholds to catch early 429 spikes (elaine)

charlie: i'm owning the immediate postmortem write-up. bob will lead the remediation (circuit breaker + retry policy). we'll schedule a 1h blameless review tomorrow.

alice: handing off to bob for long-running remediation. i'll stay on-call for 30 more mins for verification, then escalate to next oncall if needed.

bob: ack, continuing on remediation. updating runbook with steps done. please add any logs/request IDs you collect in this thread.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: key mitigations in place, error rates returned to baseline at 01:25 UTC. auto-note: severity=P2, impact=partial-degradation, duration=~27m.

alice: thanks all. nice coordination. :heart: I'll create the incident ticket in JIRA and assign follow-ups.

dana: will loop in CS to coordinate customer comms and SLA requests.

frank: customers want a short RCA and ETA for fixes. we'll coordinate via CS channel after the postmortem.

bob: adding a short checklist to runbook for future quota rollouts: feature-flagged -> canary 5% traffic -> 30m watch -> gradual rollout.

charlie: noted. I'll revert the rush PR flow that bypassed the canary for this change.

incident-bot: Pager cleared for oncall `alice` at 01:28 UTC.

alice: handing off to next oncall (bob) now — thanks team, will follow up asynchronously.
